raw_response:
I've farmed this land my whole life. My father grew wheat and corn here, and his father before him. I know this soil. I have 8 mu total, all flat, all on the same rotation I've done for 40 years: winter wheat, then summer maize. That's what this land is for. That's what the market buys.

The wheat is already in the ground — I planted it back in October. Right now it's jointing, doing fine. I'll irrigate again soon for heading, then once more at grain filling if it's dry. I'll spray for aphids and powdery mildew like I always do in May.

After I harvest wheat in June, I'll plant maize right away. I'll use Zhengdan 958 — I've used it for years, it's reliable. My neighbor tried a new hybrid last year, said the rep promised him 700 jin per mu. He got 550. I'll stick with what I know.

For fertilizer, I put down compound fertilizer at planting and topdress urea before jointing for wheat. For maize I split the urea: some at planting, the rest when it's knee-high. My son says I use too much, he heard something on the radio. But I'm not going to starve my crop. I've never had a total failure in 40 years.

I won't grow cotton. Too much work now, my back isn't what it was. Cotton prices aren't worth it anyway. Vegetables, maybe a small patch near the house for ourselves, but I won't count that.
